stat3label = [[Assist (basketball)|Assists]] | stat3value = 849 (2.5 apg) }} [[File:Shabazz Napier 2020.jpg|thumb|230px|Napier with the [[Washington Wizards]] in 2020]] '''Shabazz Bozie Napier''' (born July 14, 1991) is a Puerto Rican former professional [[basketball]] player who currently serves as a [[coach (basketball)|coaching apprentice]] for the [[Washington Wizards]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He was drafted 24th overall by the [[Charlotte Hornets]] in the [[2014 NBA draft]] and immediately traded to the [[Miami Heat]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Connecticut Huskies men's basketball|Connecticut Huskies]], and won two national championships in [[2011 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2011]] and [[2014 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2014]]. Napier was a key player for the Huskies' [[2010–11 Connecticut Huskies men's basketball team|2010–11 NCAA championship team]], as he made the Big East All Rookie team.[https://web.archive.org/web/20111122072823/http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=313240041 Shabazz Napier's triple-double helps UConn rally to beat Coppin State] Following his junior season, Napier was selected to the All-Big East first team.{{cite web|last1=Duffy|first1=Kevin|title=Napier named All-Big East First Team, Calhoun on All-Rookie Team - UConn Basketball|url=http://blog.ctnews.com/uconnbasketball/2013/03/10/napier-named-all-big-east-first-team-calhoun-on-all-rookie-team/|website=Connecticut News|publisher=Connecticut Post|access-date=29 June 2014}} In the 2013–14 season, Napier was unanimously selected for the All-AAC first team, and was named the inaugural [[American Athletic Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|American Athletic Conference Player of the Year]].{{Cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400496843|title=Shabazz Napier's triple-double lifts No. 19 UConn over Yale|work=ESPN.com|date=November 11, 2013|access-date=June 27, 2014}} He was again one of UConn's key players when they won the NCAA tournament for a second time in four years in [[2013–14 Connecticut Huskies men's basketball team|2014]] and was named as the tournament's most outstanding player.{{cite web|title=UConn's Napier named most outstanding player of Final Four|url=https://www.foxnews.com/sports/uconns-napier-named-most-outstanding-player-of-final-four/|website=Fox News|publisher=Associated Press|access-date=29 June 2014}} ==Early life== Napier was born in the [[Roxbury, Boston|Roxbury]] neighborhood of [[Boston]] to Carmen Velásquez, a native of [[Puerto Rico]], and Alex Napier, who is African American.{{cite web|url=https://www.nydailynews.com/hc-xpm-2013-11-06-hc-ss-uconn-men-napier-20131106-story.html |title=Shabazz Napier |work=Nydailynews.com|date=November 6, 2013|access-date=January 2, 2020}} He has an older sister Titania and an older brother Timmie. He grew up in Boston's [[Mission Hill, Boston|Mission Hill]] neighborhood,{{cite web|url=http://www.sportsonearth.com/article/67611648/how-shabazz-napier-has-become-connecticut-huskies-star|title=The Path to Stardom|work=SportsOnEarth.com|date=February 11, 2014|access-date=June 27, 2014|archive-date=October 8, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141008210451/http://www.sportsonearth.com/article/67611648/how-shabazz-napier-has-become-connecticut-huskies-star|url-status=dead}} and took a liking to basketball during that period.{{cite web|url=http://www.uconnhuskies.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/shabazz_napier_714048.html|title=Shabazz Napier Bio|work=UConnHuskies.com|access-date=June 27, 2014|archive-date=June 23, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180623100236/http://www.uconnhuskies.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/shabazz_napier_714048.html|url-status=dead}} ==High school career== Napier attended his first two years of high school at [[Charlestown High School]] in Boston's [[Charlestown, Boston|Charlestown]] neighborhood before transferring to [[Lawrence Academy at Groton|Lawrence Academy]] in [[Groton, Massachusetts]] and [[reclassification (education)|reclassifying]] as a junior. As a senior, Napier led Lawrence Academy to an undefeated season going 29–0 in 2010, as they won the [[New England Preparatory School Athletic Council|New England Prep]] Class C title after defeating St. Mark's finishing with 23 points, 8 steals, and 8 assists as he was named Tournament MVP. Considered a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Napier was listed as the No. 25 point guard and the No. 98 player in the nation in 2010.[https://rivals.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Shabazz-Napier-109273;_ylt=ArGGXRKfSX78.AWEetFFBErXO5B4 Shabazz Napier Recruiting Profile] In January 2014, Charlestown High School retired Napier's jersey.[http://www.nhregister.com/sports/20140130/shabazz-napier-going-back-to-where-it-all-started Shabazz Napier going back to where it all started] ==College career== ===Freshman season=== [[File:UConn's Shabazz Napier.jpg|300px|thumbnail|right|Napier dribbling around a [[pick and roll]] play setup by teammate [[Alex Oriakhi]].]] Following his prep career, Napier chose to play at the University of Connecticut under coach [[Jim Calhoun]].{{cite web|last1=Schwartz|first1=Alex|title=Blog.Northstarbball.com: Shabazz Napier Picks UConn, Attempting to Reclassify|url=http://blog.northstarbball.com/2010/04/03/shabazz-napier-picks-uconn-attempting-to-reclassify.aspx|website=Northstar Basketball Blog|access-date=29 June 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140726135105/http://blog.northstarbball.com/2010/04/03/shabazz-napier-picks-uconn-attempting-to-reclassify.aspx|archive-date=July 26, 2014|df=mdy-all}} He had a solid freshman year in 2010–11 backing up [[Kemba Walker]]. He appeared in all 41 games for the Huskies, coming off the bench averaging 7.8 points, 3.0 assists and 1.8 steals per game for the season. At the end of the regular season, Napier was named to the [[Big East Conference|Big East]] All-Rookie team along with teammate [[Jeremy Lamb]].{{cite web|title=Three Huskies Honored By Big East << CBS Connecticut|url=http://connecticut.cbslocal.com/2011/03/06/three-huskies-honored-by-big-east/|website=CBS Connecticut|publisher=CBS|access-date=28 June 2014}} Napier hit two game clinching free throws to secure a win in the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|Final Four]] against Kentucky. Napier's contribution to the team was significant, as Connecticut finished the season 32–9 (9–9 in conference play) and won both the Big East Conference Championship and National Championship in 2011. ===Sophomore season=== During the summer after his freshman year, Napier was invited to the trials for the [[2011 Summer Universiade|2011 World University Games]] team.{{cite web|last1=Keefe|first1=Gavin|title=The Day - Napier heads to tryouts, Oriakhi leaves|url=http://www.theday.com/article/20110728/INTERACT010103/110729510/0/SPORT05|website=The Day Connecticut|access-date=29 June 2014|archive-date=July 26, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140726012033/http://www.theday.com/article/20110728/INTERACT010103/110729510/0/SPORT05|url-status=dead}} Moving into the starting lineup as a sophomore for Connecticut, Napier was a preseason honorable mention All-Big East pick and a Bob Cousy Award candidate.{{cite web|last1=Bethune|first1=Ian|title=UConn Men Picked To Finish Atop Big East With Syracuse|url=https://soxanddawgs.com/huskies/articles/2011-12-big-east-mens-basketball-preseason-coaches-poll.html|website=Bloguin|date=October 19, 2011 |access-date=29 June 2014}}{{cite web|title=UConn's Shabazz Napier Candidate For Cousy Award|url=https://www.courant.com/2011/12/19/uconns-shabazz-napier-candidate-for-cousy-award-2/|website=Hartford Courant|date=December 19, 2011 |access-date=29 June 2014}} His numbers improved, as Napier averaged 13.0 points, 5.8 assists, 3.5 rebounds, and 1.6 steals per game. Napier notched his first career triple-double (the ninth in Connecticut men's basketball history) as he tallied 22 points, 12 rebounds and 13 assists against Coppin State on November 20, 2011.{{cite web|last1=Amore|first1=Dom|title=Shabazz Napier Joins List of UConn's Triple-Doubles|url=https://www.courant.com/2011/11/20/shabazz-napier-joins-list-of-uconns-triple-doubles/|website=Hartford Courant|date=November 20, 2011 |access-date=29 June 2014}} Connecticut earned a 9 seed in the NCAA Tournament, but fell short to Iowa State as the Huskies finished the season going 20–14 (8–10 in conference play). Before his junior season started, Napier considered transferring after Jim Calhoun's retirement and the team's postseason ban next season, but chose to return.{{cite web|title=UConn's Napier Considered Leaving After Calhoun Retired|url=https://zagsblog.com/uconn/uconns-napier-boatright-soldier-on-despite-postseason-ban/|website=ZagsBlog.com|date=October 18, 2012 |access-date=29 June 2014}} Connecticut hired assistant coach [[Kevin Ollie]] to replace Calhoun as head coach. ===Junior season=== Following his return, Napier along with backcourt teammate [[Ryan Boatright]] both rose to the national spotlight as they were highlighted as one of the nation's best backcourts, as the two averaged a combined 33 points and 9 assists per game, outplaying nearly every opponents' backcourt they played. He also scored his 1000th career point in a game against DePaul. Napier excelled in overtime play, scoring 55 points in 45 minutes of overtime play, as he led them to a school record 5 overtime wins.{{cite web|title=Shabazz Napier Will Return For Senior Year|url=http://www.uconnhuskies.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/042613aab.html|website=UConnhuskies.com|access-date=29 June 2014|archive-date=July 26, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140726023700/http://www.uconnhuskies.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/042613aab.html|url-status=dead}} Napier averaged 17.1 points, 4.6 assists, 4.4 rebounds, and 2.0 steals a game. Following the end of the regular season, Napier made the All-USBWA District 1 team, and was the USBWA District I Player of the Year.{{cite web|title=USBWA names All-District Teams|url=http://www.pickinsplinters.com/?p=30259|website=PickinSplinters.com|access-date=29 June 2014|archive-date=July 23, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140723140045/http://www.pickinsplinters.com/?p=30259|url-status=dead}} Napier was then chosen to the Big East All First Team, was an honorable mention for Big East Player of the Year. He led the Huskies under first year coach Kevin Ollie to a 20–10 record (10–8 in conference play) despite having no postseason eligibility. ===Senior season=== On April 26, 2013, Napier opted to return to the team for his senior year along with teammates [[Ryan Boatright]] and [[DeAndre Daniels]]. Napier said the reason he and his teammates returned is because Napier wanted to get his degree and for him and his teammates to return to the NCAA Tournament. Napier was named as a candidate for the Wooden Award, Bob Cousy Award, Naismith Award, Senior Class Award, and Oscar Robertson Trophy.{{cite web|title=Napier On List Of 23 For Cousy Award|url=http://www.uconnhuskies.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/021714aab.html|website=UConnHuskies.com|access-date=16 May 2015|archive-date=May 24, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180524003830/http://www.uconnhuskies.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/021714aab.html|url-status=dead}} Napier recorded his 2nd career triple-double (10th in UConn history) with 14 points, 11 rebounds, and 10 assists on November 11, 2013. Napier led the team to win the 2K Sports Classic Title and was named Tournament MVP. In a game against Florida, Napier hit the game winning shot as time expired. Following the end of the regular season, Napier was named a unanimous selection for the AAC All-First team, and was awarded the inaugural [[American Athletic Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|AAC Player of the Year]].{{cite web|title=UConn's Shabazz Napier Named American Athletic Conference Player of the Year|url=http://theamerican.org/news/2014/3/12/MBB_0312145520.aspx|website=TheAmerican.org|date=March 12, 2014 |publisher=American Athletic Conference|access-date=16 May 2015}} He was named the USBWA District I Player of the Year for the second straight season, and was named a first team All-American on the Wooden team, Associated Press team, USBWA and NABC, and a second team member for Sporting News. In the AAC Tournament, Napier was named to the All-Tournament team after leading the Huskies to the championship game before falling to Louisville. In the NCAA Tournament, Connecticut earned a 7 seed as Napier led them under second year coach Kevin Ollie past St. Joseph's, Villanova, Iowa State, and won the East Regional final defeating Michigan State as Napier was named the East Regional Most Outstanding Player. Napier continued to lead the Huskies through the Final Four defeating Florida before reaching the National Championship game. On April 6, Napier was named the Bob Cousy Point Guard of the Year award winner.{{cite web|title=Napier Wins 2014 Bob Cousy Award|url=http://www.uconnhuskies.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/040614aab.html|website=UConnHuskies.com|access-date=16 May 2015|archive-date=September 8, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150908005452/http://www.uconnhuskies.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/040614aab.html|url-status=dead}} On April 7, Napier and the Huskies defeated [[Kentucky Wildcats|Kentucky]] 60–54 in the National Championship game and Napier was named [[NCAA basketball tournament Most Outstanding Player|Most Outstanding Player]]. Connecticut finished the season 32–8 overall (12–6 in conference play), and Napier averaged 18.0 points, 5.9 rebounds, 4.9 assists, and 1.8 steals per game. Napier was later inducted into the Huskies of Honor. Napier, along with UConn teammates [[Niels Giffey]] and Tyler Olander, are the only Division I men's players in history to have won national championships as both freshmen and seniors.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/11832439/the-year-arrived-college-basketball-now-what |title=Welcome to 'The Year After' |first=Eamonn |last=Brennan |work=[[ESPN.com]] |date=November 10, 2014 |access-date=November 10, 2014}} He is the only player in UConn history with 1,500 points, 500 rebounds, 500 assists, and 250 steals in his career. He finished his career in fourth place on the UConn scoring list with 1,959 points, second all-time with 260 made three-point field goals and steals with 251, first in 143 games played and free throws made with 509, and third in school history with 646 assists. ==Professional career== ===Miami Heat (2014–2015)=== On June 26, 2014, Napier was selected with the 24th overall pick in the [[2014 NBA draft]] by the [[Charlotte Hornets]]. He was later traded to the [[Miami Heat]] on draft night.[https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-acquires-shabazz-napier-2014-nba-draft Heat Acquires Shabazz Napier in the 2014 NBA draft][https://www.espn.com/nba/truehoop/miamiheat/story/_/id/11142763/2014-nba-draft-miami-heat-trade-guard-shabazz-napier Heat trade up for Shabazz Napier] On July 18, 2014, he signed with the Heat after averaging 10.2 points in four [[2014 NBA Summer League|Summer League]] games for the team.[https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-sign-shabazz-napier Heat Sign Shabazz Napier] On December 13, 2014, he was assigned to the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]] of the [[NBA Development League]].[https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-assign-napier-and-whiteside-skyforce Heat Assign Napier and Whiteside to Skyforce] He was recalled on December 15,[https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-recall-napier-and-whiteside-skyforce Heat Recall Napier and Whiteside From Skyforce] reassigned on December 30,[https://www.nba.com/heat/heat-assign-shabazz-napier-skyforce Heat Assign Shabazz Napier to Skyforce] and recalled again on January 7.[https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-recall-shabazz-napier-skyforce Heat Recall Shabazz Napier From Skyforce] On February 20, he had a season-best game with 18 points, 7 rebounds and 6 assists in a 111–87 win over the [[New York Knicks]].[https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400579099 Heat rout Knicks with Bosh out, Dragic not yet available] On April 1, 2015, Napier was ruled out for the rest of the season after undergoing successful surgery to repair a [[sports hernia]].[https://www.nba.com/heat/news/shabazz-napier-undergoes-successful-surgery Shabazz Napier Undergoes Successful Surgery] He recovered in time to join the Heat's summer league team in July to compete in Orlando and Las Vegas.[https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-announce-summer-league-information Heat Announce Summer League Information] ===Orlando Magic (2015–2016)=== On July 27, 2015, Napier was traded to the [[Orlando Magic]], along with cash considerations, in exchange for a conditional 2016 second-round draft pick.{{cite news|title=Orlando Magic Acquire Guard Shabazz Napier From Heat|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/orlando-magic-acquire-guard-shabazz-napier-heat|access-date=July 27, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=July 27, 2015}} On November 11, 2015, he scored a career-high 22 points in a 101–99 win over the Los Angeles Lakers.[https://www.nba.com/games/20151111/LALORL/gameinfo.html Vucevic hits game-winner as Magic beat Lakers 101-99] ===Portland Trail Blazers (2016–2018)=== [[File:Shabazz Napier (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|Napier with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in 2018]] On 2017}} ===Brooklyn Nets (2018–2019)=== On July 17, 2018, Napier signed a two-year, $3.8 million contract with the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web |title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Shabazz Napier |url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2018/07/17/brooklyn-nets-sign-shabazz-napier |website=NBA.com |access-date=July 17, 2018 |date=July 17, 2018}} On December 29, he tied his career high with 32 points 2019}} He ended the season with averages of 9.4 points, 1.8 rebounds and 2.6 assists in 17.6 minutes.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/n/napiesh01.html|title=Shabazz Napier (2022–2023)=== On November 4, 2022, Napier was named to the opening night roster for the [[Mexico City Capitanes]].{{cite web|url=https://capitanes.gleague.nba.com/roster|title=Capitanes de Ciudad de México roster 2022-23|date=November 4, 2022|access-date=November 4, 2022}} ===Olimpia Milano (2023)=== On January 28, 2023, he signed with [[Olimpia Milano]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A]] (LBA).{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/olimpia-milano-signs-shabazz-napier/|title=Olimpia Milano signs Shabazz Napier|date=January 28, 2023|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=January 28, 2023 |last1=Carchia |first1=Emiliano }} ===Crvena zvezda (2023)=== On July 16, 2023, Napier signed a two-year deal with Serbian powerhouse [[KK Crvena zvezda|Crvena zvezda]]. His brief time in Serbia was marked by numerous controversies and extremely poor play, with many media sources eventually pointing out that Napier used various [[Scam|tricks]] and excuses to effectively place himself on a [[sabbatical leave]] during which he refused to play against any other prospective team that might hire him in the future.{{Cite web |date=2023-12-20 |title=Kako je propao Šabaz Nejpir: Priča o čoveku koji je trebalo da bude prvi adut Crvene zvezde |url=https://sportal.blic.rs/prica/kako-je-propao-sabaz-nejpir-prica-o-coveku-koji-je-trebalo-da-bude-prvi-adut-crvene-zvezde-2023121920190329049 |access-date=2025-03-05 |website=Sportal.rs |language=sr}} In December of the same year, he had a public fallout with new head coach [[Ioannis Sfairopoulos]] and fell out of the rotation. Eventually he was released from his contract on the condition that he signs only with his former club [[Olimpia Milano]]. ===Return to Olimpia Milano (2023–2024)=== On December 21, 2023, Napier signed back with [[Olimpia Milano]] under coach [[Ettore Messina]]. === Bayern Munich (2024–2025) === On September 4, 2024, Napier signed with [[FC Bayern Munich (basketball)|Bayern Munich]] of the German [[Basketball Bundesliga]] (BBL) and the [[EuroLeague]].{{Cite web |date=September 4, 2024 |title=SHABAZZ NAPIER COMPLETES THE FC BAYERN BASKETBALL ROSTER |url=https://fcbayern.com/basketball/en/news/2024-25/09/top-guard-shabazz-napier-completes-the-fc-bayern-basketball-roster}} On August 17, 2025, Napier parted ways with the German club. ==National team career== Napier's mother and manager, Carmen Velásquez, is [[Puerto Rican people|Puerto Rican]], which made him directly eligible to represent [[Puerto Rico]] under [[FIBA]] regulations. On February 19, 2012, it was announced that following formal meetings with personnel of the [[Puerto Rican Basketball Federation]], he had presented the required documentation and agreed to join the [[Puerto Rico national basketball team]]'s practice for its next tournament, the 2012 Centrobasket. This tournament served as qualifier for the 2013 FIBA Americas Tournament.{{cite web |url=https://www.primerahora.com/deportes/baloncesto/nota/contentoflormelendezconharklessyshabazznapier-616113/|title=Contento Flor Meléndez con Harkless y Shabazz Napier|work=PrimeraHora.com |language=es |date=February 21, 2012 |access-date=February 21, 2012}} He did not participate in the [[2012 Centrobasket]] due to injury. In December 2013, the then [[Puerto Rico men's national basketball team]] coach [[Paco Olmos]] held a meeting with Napier and Velásquez, where his program was explained.[http://www.noticel.com/noticia/153212/paco-olmos-ya-hablo-con-shabazz-napier.html Paco Olmos ya habló con Shabazz Napier] The coach referred to this meeting as "constructive" and later noted that both sides kept good communication.{{Cite web |url=http://www.basquetplus.com/nota-22099-olmos-hemos-hecho-todo-y-mas-para-conseguir-a-napier |title=Olmos: "Hemos hecho todo y más para conseguir a Napier" |access-date=May 9, 2014 |archive-date=September 23, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150923184333/http://www.basquetplus.com/nota-22099-olmos-hemos-hecho-todo-y-mas-para-conseguir-a-napier |url-status=dead }} When questioned about the possibility of joining Puerto Rico in 2014, Napier responded by saying "I would love to go and have that experience. It would be something unique and that will definitely help my game for the goals I have set. It will be an honor. [...] Everything I am today as a player, I owe to [UCONN]. And as a person, to the education of my mother, who would be proud if I play for Puerto Rico."{{Cite web |url=http://www.fibaamericas.com/en/noticiasread4.asp?r=5748B8AC4B3B40E38FDB10C0564BA0E2 |title=SPAIN2014 - Napier: "It will be an honor" |access-date=May 9, 2014 |archive-date=March 4, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304052905/http://www.fibaamericas.com/en/noticiasread4.asp?r=5748B8AC4B3B40E38FDB10C0564BA0E2 |url-status=dead }} ==Coaching career== On October 20, 2025, the [[Washington Wizards]] hired Napier to serve as a coaching apprentice under head coach [[Brian Keefe]].{{Cite web|title=Shabazz Napier starts new chapter as NBA
